files.title: Files
files.subtitle: Browse the files and data for OpenMasjidOS and your apps.
files.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
files.protectedHint: This is OpenMasjidOS's own data, so it's kept private. Your settings and keys are managed in Settings, and each app is managed from its own page.

ports.title: Port already in use
ports.body: This app wants a port that something else is already using. Pick a free one and we'll set it up for you.

auth.setupSubtitle: Let's create your admin account to get started.
auth.loginSubtitle: Sign in to manage your masjid's apps.
auth.name: Your name
auth.emailHint: Where OpenMasjidOS sends alerts (like an app going offline). This is not your sign-in.
auth.passwordHint: Use at least 12 characters — this account controls the whole server.
auth.restoreHint: Moving from another machine? Restore your backup — your account, settings and all app data come back. No need to create a new account.
auth.passwordTooShort: Your password needs to be at least 12 characters.
auth.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
auth.resetIntro: You'll need terminal access to the machine running OpenMasjidOS — at it directly or over SSH. Then run:
auth.resetOutro: Then come back here and sign in. Your apps and data are untouched.

dashboard.noAppsBody: Browse the App Store to find apps for your masjid — prayer times, announcements, donation pages, and more.
dashboard.diskWarnBody: Free up space by removing apps or files you no longer need, so your apps keep running smoothly.
dashboard.updateTitle: A new version is available — v{{version}}
dashboard.updateBody: Update OpenMasjidOS to get the latest features and fixes. Your apps and their data are left untouched.
dashboard.appPendingTitle_one: 1 app is not on your selected channel yet
dashboard.appPendingTitle_other: {{count}} apps are not on your selected channel yet
dashboard.devChannelBody: This masjid is running what we're still building, not a tested release. Updates arrive here the same way as on Stable — you'll be told when there's a new build. Switch back to Stable in Settings whenever you like.

appCard.removeBody: This turns the app off and removes it from your dashboard.
appCard.removeData: Also delete this app's data (cannot be undone)
appCard.upToDate: This app is up to date.
appCard.updateBody: Version {{latest}} is available — you have {{current}}. The app will restart; its data is kept.

store.title: App Store
store.subtitle: Find and install apps for your masjid
store.emptyHint: The app catalog is on its way. Check back soon.
store.installingHint: Installing… downloading the app, this can take a minute.
store.installError: Something went wrong while installing. Please try again.
store.shareOnline: Share this app over the internet
store.shareOnlineHint: {{name}} works best when people can reach it from home — for example so parents can sign in, or so links you email them actually open. Leave this off to keep it on your masjid's network only.
store.shareOnlineNoRemote: Remote access isn't switched on yet, so this app won't have an internet address until you set it up.
store.shareOnlineChangeLater: You can change this any time in Settings → Remote access, or on the app's own page.
store.stripeNone: No Stripe accounts yet — add one first:

custom.title: Install a custom app
custom.warning: Custom apps come from outside the OpenMasjidOS store and aren't reviewed by us. A bad or untrusted file can break your server or expose it. Only install ones you trust.
custom.name: App name
custom.dangersTitle: This app asks for powerful permissions:
custom.refusalsBody: It tries to open another app's data, which is never allowed — not even if you agree to the risk. Ask whoever gave you this file to remove it.
custom.riskAck: I understand the risk and want to install it anyway.
custom.shareOnlineHint: Let people outside your masjid open {{name}} over the internet. Leave this off and it stays on your network only — you can change it later in Settings.
custom.nameRequired: Please give the app a name.
custom.composeRequired: Please paste a Docker Compose file.
custom.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
custom.disabledBody: Turn on "Allow custom apps" in Settings → Advanced to install community apps or your own Compose files.

community.title: 3rd Party Apps
community.subtitle: Install community apps from app stores, or paste your own Docker Compose file.
community.noRepos: No app stores yet. Add a CasaOS-compatible repository to browse community apps.
community.noApps: No apps found in your app stores.
community.addRepoError: Couldn't read that app store. Check the link points to a CasaOS-compatible repository.
community.casaNote: Tip: use CasaOS-compatible app stores. Paste the link to the store's repository (a .zip or GitHub repo URL).
community.thirdPartyNotice: This is a community app from outside the official store — it isn't reviewed by us. Only install apps from sources you trust.
community.installing: Installing… downloading the app, this can take a minute.

appDetail.internetShare: Share this app over the internet
appDetail.internetAt: Anyone with the link can reach it at {{url}}
appDetail.internetPending: Shared — it will get an internet address once Remote access is set up.
appDetail.internetOff: This app is only reachable on your masjid's own network.
appDetail.internetSettingsLink: Manage all shared apps in Settings → Remote access

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Customize your dashboard
settings.wallpaperImageHint: Paste an image URL to use your own wallpaper. Overrides the preset above.
settings.logoHint: Add your masjid's logo. It appears on the emails your masjid sends (alerts and, when an app supports it, receipts) and as the avatar on notification messages.
settings.logoFormats: PNG, JPG, or WebP · up to 1 MB
settings.dashboardNameHint: Shown in the greeting. Leave blank for the default.
settings.showSplash: Play the welcome animation on load
settings.languageHint: More translations are on the way — only English is complete for now.
settings.accountEmailHint: Where OpenMasjidOS sends alerts (like an app going offline). You sign in with your username, not this.
settings.emailHint: Set up SMTP or Resend once. OpenMasjidOS emails you alerts, and apps can send email (donation receipts, parent notices) through it — no app ever sees your credentials.
settings.emailSecretKept: •••••• (saved — paste a new one to replace)
settings.emailFromInvalid: Enter a valid email address (e.g. no-reply@yourmasjid.org).
settings.emailTestFailed: Could not send the test email. Check your settings.
settings.alertsHint: For each alert, choose where it goes — your email, your webhook, both, or neither. Everything is on by default. (These go to you, the admin. Emails to donors/parents are sent by the app itself.)
settings.alertsNone: No alerts yet — they appear here as you install apps.
settings.customAppsHint: Adds a "3rd Party App" button to the App Store for installing community apps or your own Docker Compose files. Only turn this on if you know what you're doing.
settings.webTerminalHint: Adds an "Open shell" option to each app so you can run commands inside it from the browser. Powerful — anyone signed in gets shell access to your apps.
settings.rootTerminalHint: Adds a root shell into the OpenMasjidOS core itself (full control of Docker on this server). Only enable this if you understand the risk.
settings.eagerBody: We love how keen you are for the next release — really. But please allow us a little time between updates; we're only human, and good things take a moment to bake. If you'd like speedy, jam-packed releases, please consider supporting the project — it genuinely helps us ship faster. JazākAllāhu khayran.
settings.reconnectHint: If you've moved this machine to a different network, use this to point your apps back at the dashboard.
settings.reconnectDone_zero: Your apps were already pointed at the right address.
settings.reconnectDone_one: Network settings refreshed. 1 app needs restarting to pick up the new address.
settings.reconnectDone_other: Network settings refreshed. {{count}} apps need restarting to pick up the new address.
settings.channelMigrateProgress: Moving {{name}} to {{label}} — app {{current}} of {{total}}. Each app restarts for a few seconds; its settings and data are kept.
settings.channelMigrateDone: All your apps are now on {{label}}.
settings.channelMigrateOs: Your apps are on {{label}}. Now updating OpenMasjidOS itself — this page will reconnect when it comes back.
settings.channelHint: Which version of OpenMasjidOS and your apps this masjid runs. Stable is tested and recommended.
settings.channelDevConfirmBody: Development builds are what we're still working on. They are not tested, they change every day, and they can stop your apps working — including your prayer times display.
settings.channelDevConfirmCost: Coming back to Stable later may mean reinstalling your apps, and anything a Development version saved might not work on Stable. Only do this if you're happy to fix things yourself.
settings.channelStableConfirmBody: Your apps will be put back to their Stable versions. Their data is kept, but anything added by a Development version may not work properly on Stable — Development can be ahead of Stable in ways that don't go backwards cleanly.
settings.channelStableConfirmCost: We can't undo Development-only changes to your apps' data. If something looks wrong afterwards, restore a backup from before you switched.
settings.channelPendingTitle_one: 1 app is still on the other channel
settings.channelPendingTitle_other: {{count}} apps are still on the other channel
settings.channelPendingBody: Update them so everything runs the same channel. Their settings and data are kept.
settings.channelDevNote: Development builds are numbered too, so you're told when a new one is ready and update it exactly like a Stable release.
settings.sslHint: The dashboard is served over HTTPS.
settings.sslSelfSignedNote: Using a self-signed certificate (valid until {{date}}). Browsers show a one-time "not secure" warning per device — click Advanced → Proceed once. Upload your own certificate from a real domain to remove the warning.
settings.sslRecoveredCustom: On {{date}} the certificate you uploaded could no longer be read, so OpenMasjidOS made a temporary one to keep this dashboard reachable. Please upload yours again below. (What went wrong: {{reason}}.)
settings.sslRecoveredSelfSigned: On {{date}} this server's certificate could no longer be read, so OpenMasjidOS made a new one. Your devices may ask you to accept it once more. (What went wrong: {{reason}}.)
settings.sslRegenerated: A new certificate was generated and is now live.
settings.sslUploadBody: Paste your certificate and private key in PEM format (including the BEGIN/END lines). They're applied immediately.
settings.sslSaved: Your certificate is installed and live.
settings.sshHint: Add an SSH public key to log in to this machine as root. Anyone with the matching private key can then access the server — only add keys you trust.
settings.sshKeyAdded: SSH key added. You can now sign in as root with that key.
settings.sshPasswordNote: To allow root login with a password instead, run this on the machine (then reconnect):
settings.sshPasswordCmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/; s/^#\?PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart ssh sshd 2>/dev/null || sudo service ssh restart
settings.freeSpaceHint: Removes downloaded app images that no app is using anymore (e.g. apps you've removed). Your installed apps and their data are not affected.
settings.rebootHint: Restart the whole machine. The dashboard and all apps go offline for a minute or two while it boots back up.
settings.rebootConfirmBody: This restarts the entire machine. The dashboard and every app will be offline for a minute or two, then come back on their own. Your data is untouched.
settings.rebooting: Rebooting… the server is going down. This page will be unavailable until it's back (usually a minute or two) — then refresh.
settings.freedNone: Nothing to clean up — you're all tidy.
settings.showClock: Show a clock on the dashboard
settings.backupHint: Saves a copy of your settings and app data as a single file.
settings.offsiteBackupsHint: Automatically copy your backup — your settings plus every app's data — to Google Drive or a NAS, on a schedule, so a copy lives safely off the machine.
settings.backupContentsBody: A backup holds everything: the personal details your apps store about people, your saved payment keys, your email password and your remote-access token — and the file itself is not password-protected. Keep it somewhere only you can reach, and treat it as carefully as you would the server itself.
settings.backupRetentionHint: Once there are more than this many on the destination, the oldest are removed.
settings.backupDriveIntro: Google won't let a device on your local network connect to Drive with one click — the sign-in has to happen on a computer with a web browser. It only takes a minute:
settings.backupDriveStep1: On any computer, install the free rclone tool.
settings.backupDriveStep2: Open a terminal, run this, and sign in to Google when your browser opens:
settings.backupDriveStep3: Paste the whole token line it prints below — that's it.
settings.backupKeyOptional: Use a private key instead of a password
settings.backupFolderHint: The folder on the destination to keep backups in (it's created if it doesn't exist).
settings.paymentsHint: Add your Stripe account here once and any app that takes card payments (donations, kiosk…) can use it — no need to paste your keys into each app. Give each account a name and pick it inside the app.
settings.stripeWebhookHint: Optional — only needed if an app verifies Stripe webhooks. In Stripe, open Workbench → Webhooks (older accounts: Developers → Webhooks), open the endpoint for your app, and click “Reveal” / “Click to reveal” the signing secret (starts with whsec_). It's unique per endpoint and differs between test and live mode.
settings.stripeKeepBlank: Leave blank to keep the saved one
settings.stripeGuideTitle: Where do I find my Stripe keys?
settings.stripeGuideWebhook: Webhook signing secret (optional, only if an app verifies webhooks): Stripe → Workbench → Webhooks (older accounts: Developers → Webhooks) → add/open your endpoint → “Reveal” the signing secret (whsec_…). It's per-endpoint and differs between test and live mode.
settings.stripeGuideTest: Tip: use test keys (pk_test… / sk_test…) while trying things out, then switch to live keys to take real donations.
settings.remoteAccessHint: Reach your masjid's apps from anywhere over your own domain — no port forwarding, no public IP. Create a Cloudflare Tunnel, paste its token + your domain here, and the OS runs it. Apps automatically learn their public address.
settings.cfStopped: Tunnel is set up but turned off.
settings.cfNoToken: Add a tunnel token to turn this on.
settings.cfDomainHint: The full public hostname your tunnel serves — the EXACT one you create in Cloudflare (e.g. omos.example.org). Used as-is, no https://.
settings.cfTokenSet: A token is saved — paste a new one to replace it
settings.cfTokenHint: From the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard → Networks → Tunnels → your tunnel → install token (the long string after 'run --token'). Kept private; never shown again.
settings.cfGuideTitle: How to set this up (step by step)
settings.cfStep1b: → Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel → choose Cloudflared.
settings.cfStep2: Name it (e.g. "openmasjid") and save. On the install screen, copy the token — the long string right after --token in the command shown. Paste it above with your domain, then turn Remote access on.
settings.cfStep3: Open the tunnel's Public Hostnames tab and add ONE route (the OS routes each app for you — no per-app rows):
settings.cfStep3Host: Public hostname: set Subdomain + Domain so together they equal EXACTLY the domain you entered above —
settings.cfStep3Service: Path: leave empty. Service → Type: HTTP (NOT HTTPS), URL: localhost:{{port}}
settings.cfHttpWarn: Important: pick Type HTTP — not HTTPS. Port {{port}} is a plain-HTTP port, so choosing HTTPS gives a 502 error. Leave “No TLS Verify” off; it isn't needed.
settings.cfStep4: Cloudflare adds the DNS record automatically. Your apps are then reachable at the addresses below — OpenMasjidOS sends each path to the right app.
settings.cfRoutesTitle: Your apps will be reachable at:
settings.cfExposedOn: This app is now reachable from the internet.
settings.cfExposedOff: This app is now on your network only.
settings.cfRoutesHint: Edit an app's path here (e.g. “donate”). You do NOT add these in Cloudflare — the single route above sends everything to OpenMasjidOS, which routes each path to the right app.
settings.restoreConfirmBody: This replaces your current settings and app data with the backup, then restarts your apps and the dashboard. This can't be undone — download a backup first if you're unsure.
settings.notificationsHint: Let your apps send a message to Slack, Discord, or any webhook (e.g. a new donation or announcement). Set it up once here; apps you install can use it. The webhook is kept private — apps never see it.
settings.notificationsUrlHint: Paste the incoming-webhook URL from Slack or Discord, or any address that accepts a JSON POST.
settings.notificationsLabelHint: A short name shown at the start of each message — e.g. your masjid's name.
settings.notificationsTestSent: Test sent — check your Slack, Discord, or webhook.
settings.notificationsTestFailed: Couldn't send. Check the webhook URL and that notifications are turned on.
settings.sourceCodeHint: OpenMasjidOS is free and open source (AGPL-3.0).
settings.accountPhoneHint: Where OpenMasjidOS sends WhatsApp alerts, and the number the test message goes to. Include the country code. Leave empty to turn it off. This is not a sign-in.
settings.whatsappHint: Send alerts and app messages over WhatsApp, through a gateway running on your own server. Install OpenWA from the App Store, then enter the key and session name you gave it.
settings.whatsappRiskTitle: Please read this before linking a phone
settings.whatsappRiskBody: WhatsApp does not officially allow this, and the number you link can be restricted or blocked — there is no way to make that risk zero. OpenMasjidOS spaces messages out and keeps quiet hours to reduce it, and email always keeps working as a fallback.
settings.whatsappSessionHint: A label for this masjid’s WhatsApp connection. OpenMasjidOS creates the session for you — you never need to open OpenWA to find an id.
settings.whatsappKeyHint: The same key you entered when installing OpenWA (the OPENWA_API_KEY setting). Stored on this server only and never shown again. Note: OpenWA only reads that key the first time it starts, so changing it here later will not change the gateway’s key — reinstall OpenWA if you need to rotate it.
settings.whatsappUrlHint: Leave empty if you installed OpenWA from the App Store — it is found for you. Only fill this in if the gateway runs on another machine.
settings.whatsappTestSent: Test message sent. Check your WhatsApp.
settings.whatsappLinkHint: Enter the number to send from, then open WhatsApp on that phone → Settings → Linked devices → Link with phone number, and type the code below.
settings.whatsappStateReady: Connected and ready. {{queued}} message(s) waiting to send.
settings.whatsappStateNotLinked: The gateway is running, but no phone is linked yet. Use “Link your phone” below.
settings.whatsappRiskCost: Use a spare number the masjid keeps for this — never a volunteer's personal phone or your main published line. Email stays your reliable channel.
settings.whatsappGatewayInstallHint: OpenMasjidOS sends WhatsApp messages through OpenWA, which runs on your own server. Install it to continue — it only appears in the App Store while this is switched on.
settings.whatsappGatewayOpenHint: Link your phone here in OpenMasjidOS, not in OpenWA — OpenMasjidOS looks after the connection for you. Open OpenWA only if you want to read or reply to chats yourself.
settings.whatsappGatewayStopped: It isn't running at the moment.
settings.whatsappLinkNumberHint: The number messages will be sent FROM.
settings.whatsappStateRestricted: WhatsApp has placed a restriction on this number ({{detail}}). Messages may not get through.
settings.phoneHint: Pick the country, then type the rest of the number as you'd normally write it.
settings.phoneHintOther: Type the whole number including its country code.
settings.whatsappStateBadKey: The gateway is running but rejected the API key. Re-paste the key you set when installing OpenWA.
settings.whatsappStateNoSession: Gateway found, no connection created yet. Use “Link your phone” below and OpenMasjidOS will set it up.
settings.whatsappStateProblem: The phone connection needs attention (“{{detail}}”). Try linking it again.

update.title: Updating OpenMasjidOS
update.dontClose: Please leave this open until it finishes.
update.restarting: Applying the update and restarting — reconnecting…

confirm.stripeRemoveBody: Apps that take payments through this account will stop working straight away.
confirm.stripeRemoveCost: OpenMasjidOS can't show you the secret key again, so you'd need to create a new one in Stripe and enter it here along with the webhook secret.
